question: What is a major clinical reason for keeping bed linen tight and wrinkle-free?

options.A: To make the ward look clean and tidy for visitors
options.B: To prevent pressure ulcers by reducing skin friction
options.C: To ensure the mattress lasts much longer over time
options.D: To help the patient sit up easier without sliding

explanation: Wrinkles and loose sheets create friction and shearing forces against the skin, which easily damages tissue and leads to pressure sores. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h1)

question: How should a midwife primarily view the task of making a patient's bed?

options.A: As an optional comfort measure requested by the doctor
options.B: As an administrative duty required for hospital records
options.C: As a routine domestic chore meant for junior staff only
options.D: As an essential clinical intervention for patient safety

explanation: Bed making directly impacts infection control, skin integrity, and overall patient comfort, making it a core clinical nursing skill. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why must a midwife NEVER shake used bed sheets in the ward?

options.A: It stretches the fabric and ruins the elastic edges
options.B: It creates too much noise for resting patients nearby
options.C: It spreads infectious dust and microorganisms into the air
options.D: It tangles the linens and makes sorting difficult later

explanation: Shaking linens releases dust, skin flakes, and microorganisms into the surrounding air, increasing the risk of airborne cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which body mechanics practice helps protect the midwife's back during bed making?

options.A: Reaching as far across the mattress as possible to save time
options.B: Bending at the knees and keeping a wide base of support
options.C: Keeping the knees completely locked while pulling heavy sheets
options.D: Lowering the bed all the way to the floor for better leverage

explanation: Proper body mechanics require using large leg muscles by bending the knees and maintaining a stable base, which protects the lower back from strain. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h2)

question: Where is the safest place to temporarily put clean linen while preparing a bed?

options.B: On a clean bedside chair or overbed table
options.C: Directly on the floor next to the laundry bag
options.D: On the foot of the neighboring patient's bed

explanation: Clean linen must be kept off the floor and away from other beds to prevent picking up dirt and microorganisms. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary benefit of gathering all bed-making supplies before starting the procedure?

options.A: It saves time and prevents leaving the patient unattended
options.B: It keeps the room temperature stable for the patient
options.C: It stops the mattress from sagging in the middle
options.D: It ensures the dirty linen hamper is completely empty

explanation: Having all supplies ready avoids interruptions and prevents the need to walk away from an unsafe situation or an exposed patient. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the correct way to remove dirty linen when stripping an unoccupied bed?

options.A: Shake each sheet vigorously to air out the mattress
options.B: Pull all the sheets off quickly with one fast yank
options.C: Fold the sheets into neat squares while still on the bed
options.D: Roll each piece inward to trap any debris or skin flakes

explanation: Rolling linens inward keeps skin cells, hair, and dust contained within the fabric rather than scattering them into the environment. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h4)

question: You finish making an unoccupied bed for a postpartum mother who is currently walking in the hallway. What final safety action should you take?

options.A: Pull all the top covers tightly to the very top of the frame
options.B: Leave the wheels unlocked so staff can move it easily
options.C: Raise the bed to its highest level so it is ready for use
options.D: Leave the bed in a low position with the wheels locked

explanation: Leaving an empty bed in the lowest position with locked wheels ensures patient safety when they return and attempt to get back in. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h4)

question: What critical safety precaution must a midwife take on the FAR side of the bed when making an occupied bed?

options.A: Ask a relative to hold the patient's hand
options.B: Raise the side rail on that opposite side
options.C: Lower the bed frame all the way to the floor
options.D: Place a heavy weight on the mattress edge

explanation: Raising the side rail opposite the working midwife prevents the patient from accidentally rolling out of bed while being turned. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important to talk through each step of the process when making an occupied bed?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays completely awake throughout
options.B: To prove to clinical supervisors that you know the steps
options.C: To distract the patient from pain or discomfort
options.D: To reduce patient anxiety and gain their cooperation

explanation: Patients often feel vulnerable and disoriented when being rolled and having their bedding changed; communication reassures them and secures their help. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the purpose of creating a toe pleat in the top bed linen?

options.A: To prevent pressure and foot drop on the patient's toes
options.B: To allow extra airflow underneath the bed covers
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to pull the covers up
options.D: To hide unsightly wrinkles at the bottom of the mattress

explanation: Heavy bed linens pressing down on the feet can cause toe pressure and lead to foot drop, which a loose toe pleat successfully prevents. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h6)

question: You have just finished making an occupied bed for a mother who had a Caesarean section yesterday. What final action is most critical before you walk away?

options.A: Ensure the call bell is within her easy reach
options.B: Open the ward windows to let in fresh air
options.C: Ask her to stand up to test the mattress firmness
options.D: Remove all pillows so she lies completely flat

explanation: Patients with fresh surgical incisions or restricted movement must always have their call bell within reach so they can summon assistance safely. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h6)
